subject: Private endpoint outbound accountability & minimal IP set for HeliosPay
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliospay.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@heliospay.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private endpoints - outbound IP minimal ask

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team needs a minimal, auditable list of Redwood public egress IPs and a short explanation of which service endpoints those IPs map to. They also want clarity on:
- whether Redwood initiates any outbound connections other than standard HTTPS to your control plane or telemetry endpoints,
- what retries/backoff behaviors exist so we can align firewall timeouts, and
- a primary contact for emergency egress changes.

Can you provide a compact IP set we can put into our enterprise firewall (we try to keep ACLs small)? Preferably a CSV with an owner and a one-line reason per row.

Tom
Security Operations
HeliosPay

[Helios internal request id: HP-Sec-2026-117]

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliospay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints - outbound IP minimal ask

Tom — thanks, we can do that. Attached is a compact CSV that covers the minimal public egress addresses used by the Redwood Private control plane and optional telemetry/metrics endpoints. High-level notes: 

- Minimal intent: allow only these public IPs from your firewall/NAT gateway for outbound to Redwood control/ops endpoints. All model inference traffic for "Private" deployments stays in your VPC when you choose the on-prem runtime; control-plane interactions (model manifest, rollouts, metrics) are over HTTPS.
- Protocols/ports: 443 (HTTPS) only for control plane and metrics; 5222/5223 are not used. Our runtime will not initiate arbitrary outbound TCP/UDP beyond TLS.
- Retries/backoff: exponential backoff with jitter; default max retry window is ~5 minutes for transient failures. We recommend firewall TCP idle timeouts >= 120s for long-polling and 300s for troubleshooting.
- DNS: we use SNI-friendly hostnames; if you must restrict by hostname, allow outbound DNS resolution to your internal resolvers pointing to the Redwood hostnames listed in the CSV.
- Emergency contact: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com (NOC), primary on-call 24/7. PGP fingerprint included in the attached PDF for signed change notifications.

I'm attaching: 1) redwood-private-egress-minimal-ips.csv (columns: ip_cidr,service,target_hostname,owner,reason), 2) egress-roles-and-responsibilities.pdf (short runbook).

If HeliosPay prefers an S3-signed manifest or a periodic webhook announcing IP rotations, we can add that to the SOW.

Best,
Chloe
Network Security Lead
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-private-egress-minimal-ips.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: egress-roles-and-responsibilities.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@heliospay.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoints - outbound IP minimal ask

Tom — technical follow-up with the actual minimal set (also in CSV attachment). Notes inline: 

Minimal egress IPs (example):
- 34.211.182.12/32 – control.redwood-inference.com – control-plane API (HTTPS) 
- 52.201.44.83/32 – metrics.redwood-inference.com – telemetry/metrics ingest (HTTPS, optional)
- 3.132.55.9/32 – updates.redwood-inference.com – model manifest and rollout notifications (HTTPS)

Design decisions and mitigations:
- We keep this list intentionally small and static for the pilot window. IPs are announced via a signed weekly manifest and a webhook you can subscribe to.
- If you prefer hostname/SNI allowlisting only, validate SNI at the firewall edge; we still recommend IP-based ACLs for higher-assurance customers.
- TLS: mutual TLS is available for the telemetry channel if you require cert-based client auth. Control plane supports token-based auth only.
- Failure modes: when outbound connectivity to control plane is blocked, the on-prem runtime will continue serving in offline mode for cached models; administrative actions (rollouts, config changes) will be delayed. We surface an alarm to your pager via the configured incident webhook.

Next steps:
1) Helios to confirm they will allow the three IPs above for the pilot test and provide contact for firewall change window.
2) We will publish the signed manifest to the Confluence link and enable webhook delivery to a Helios endpoint.
3) Marissa will confirm PS inclusion for weekly manifests in the pilot SOW.

-ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
